children: Australian shares fell more than 1% on Tuesday and were on track for their biggest drop in nearly three weeks, as financials and commodity-linked stocks overshadowed gains in tech shares, while National Australia Bank unveiled a major restructuring plan.

Selling was broad-based in miners and banks, with softer commodity prices hurting miners and energy firms and National Australia Bank's
restructuring programme adding pressure to lenders.

National Australia Bank said it would cut up to 2,500 jobs, or about 6% of its workforce, in 2027 to simplify its operations as the country's top business lender grapples with a more challenging outlook for credit growth. Its shares gave up early gains to trade 1.9% lower, tracking weakness in the sector.
